hypotheses.justification: The statement only uses `PQuot p I`, `PSimple p I` and `≃*`. In Definitions.lean (`variable {G : Type} [Group G]`), `PQuot p L := ↥L ⧸ GLAPPrimeCore p ↥L` and `PSimple p L := PQuot p L ⧸ center (PQuot p L)` need only `Group G`. `GLAPPrimeCore p H` is defined for any `[Group H]`, and its normality instance `GLAPPrimeCore.normal` also needs only `Group`. So the statement elaborates and is true without `Finite G`. `Finite G` is taken only as an auto-included instance variable, and it is used only because the proof calls `nonempty_pSimple_congr`, which sits in a section with `[Finite G]`. That lemma's own proof is `⟨QuotientGroup.congr _ _ e (Subgroup.map_center_eq e)⟩`, which uses no finiteness. `Subgroup.map_center_eq` is a general Mathlib lemma for `MulEquivClass`. The same argument appears finiteness-free in `Inputs256d2.lean`. So after `omit [Finite G] in`, the proof `⟨QuotientGroup.congr _ _ F (Subgroup.map_center_eq F)⟩` works. The shadowed `{p : ℕ}` variable is not an argument, since the theorem rebinds `p`.
